title: Screenreader spin-up and reduced motion guidance — grooming notes
content:
Context: This is a working doc for grooming UX + implementation patterns around: screen reader cold start (spin-up), aria-live announcement strategies for toasts and long-running operations, and respecting reduced-motion prefs across console microinteractions. Goal is to produce 1) a concise guidance section for designers, 2) a small set of component API changes for the component library, and 3) acceptance criteria for engineering tickets. Problem statements (observed in research + support): - Some customers report that first toast after a route load is not announced by VoiceOver until the user interacts (perceived as missed errors). - Animated list transitions cause cognitive load for keyboard users who rely on predictability; several users request a reduced-motion toggle for the console workspaces. - Long-running job status updates flood screenreaders when naively announced (spammy), while single announcements sometimes skip important state changes. Design proposals (high level): 1) Screenreader spin-up handshake: when a route initializes, components that will announce (toasts, job status) should wait for a short, deterministic "spin-up" window (150–350ms) before firing an aria-live message. That allows AT engines time to attach. If an immediate critical error occurs during load, surface inline visual error + an unobtrusive badge that will be announced after spin-up. 2) Toast announcement policy: toasts should default to aria-live="polite" with a max re-announcement suppression window of 5s. Important-to-announce toasts (errors with action) use role="alert" or aria-live="assertive" but must be deduped: if same error appears repeatedly within 10s, combine into one announcement and add "(repeated)" in text for context. 3) Reduced motion plumbing: Respect prefers-reduced-motion at token level. Provide motion tokens: motion.duration.short, motion.duration.medium, motion.scale. Component-level API accepts motionMode: "auto"|"reduce"|"force" and falls back to prefers-reduced-motion. For React wrapper: . Wireframe/interaction notes: - Job card state transitions (queued -> running -> failed/succeeded): update pattern should batch announcements: only announce first transition (queued), then final state after completion, unless explicit error encountered. Provide visually visible timeline with aria-describedby referencing summary text. - Modal open microinteraction: reduce duration to 120ms or disable when reduced-motion is true. Ensure focus trap is established before any non-decorative animations start. - Collapsible sidebar: instead of slide animation, use height/opacity cross-fade when reduced-motion. Keyboard users should be able to toggle with space/enter; ensure aria-expanded is updated synchronously. Component library API changes (proposed): - toast component: add props {announce: "auto"|"polite"|"assertive", dedupeKey?: string, dedupeWindowMs?: number} - Implementation: internal dedupe map by dedupeKey string, default window 10000ms. - live-region util: expose createLiveRegion({politeness, container?}) to centralize spin-up logic and suppression rules. - motion tokens file: tokens/motion.json with named durations and a helper useMotionMode() hook. Accessibility acceptance criteria (for tickets): - First toast on route load is announced within 500ms to VoiceOver on iOS Safari in at least one manual QA run. Document environment and steps. - When prefers-reduced-motion is enabled (OS setting), all microinteraction durations are <= 120ms or replaced by instant change. No component should animate more than 3 times in a 20s window. - Repeated identical toasts within 10s are announced once; UI shows repeat count badge. - Job status announcements do not exceed 1 announcement per 6s per job (unless error). Edge cases and unresolved questions: - How to handle AT that ignores aria-live until user focuses on document (some Safari versions). Fallback: surface visually persistent but unobtrusive status chip in header with aria-live to ensure it is reachable. - Internationalization: announcement strings should prefer short, semantic copies. Where possible include translatable placeholders (e.g., "{name} failed") not full sentences concatenated at runtime. - Native mobile web quirks: iOS VoiceOver often suppresses announcements if the page just loaded. We may need to add a hidden focusable anchor that receives focus briefly then returns focus — needs experimentation and accessibility review. Next steps / owners: - Engineering spike: Jonas to prototype live-region util + toast dedupe (JIRA-RI-2871). Estimated 3d. - Design: Asha to generate two microinteraction wireframes (normal vs reduced motion) for modal, toast, and list transitions. Due 2026-11-12. - QA: Diego to author a small test plan describing manual steps across VoiceOver and NVDA. Include device/OS matrix. Backlog grooming notes (priority and sizing): - RI-2871 (live-region util + toast API) - P0 for next sprint - 3 pts - RI-2872 (motion tokens + MotionContext) - P1 - 5 pts (needs design signoff) - RI-2873 (job announcement batching) - P1 - 2 pts - RI-2874 (conservative mobile fallback experiments) - spike - 2 pts Quick prototype snippets (notes, not final code): - ARIA:
{message}
- Dedupe: dedupeKey = hash(message + actionId) Open invites: please add examples of problematic toasts you've seen (copy), and any telemetry showing missed toasts. Comments from earlier sync (inline): - Diego: add telemetry hooks so we can count announce attempts vs visible toasts. - Asha: prefer a visual "badge" pattern for repeated messages rather than changing toast copy. - Jonas: will prototype a small microbenchmark for spin-up timings on real devices. Revision history: - 2026-11-02 initial draft by Maya - 2026-11-05 added dedupe proposal and ticket mapping - 2026-11-08 added acceptance criteria and owners
